liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Morning Dew** (4 reviews): Garcia puts everything on the line in a Dew rated among the best of the 1990s; Bruce's piano is stunning and draws out Garcia's best; the crescendo is overwhelming [12][13][18][22]
- **He's Gone** (3 reviews): A ripping Phil and Bobby jam with the drums after He's Gone is the reviewer's favorite part; The jams into and out of He's Gone, plus drums and space, become striking soundscapes [14][19][21]
- **Dark Star Jam** (3 reviews): A subtle transition from Space into the Dark Star theme leads into the Morning Dew; The Dark Star jam mostly sets up the Dew; it is good but not exceptional [12][14][17]
- **Brown-Eyed Women** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls it sloppy, nearly falling apart in places; Reviewer says it is mangled here, despite usually being a favorite first-set tune [17][21]
- **Help On The Way** (1 review): The Help>Slip>Frank opener is described as sweet [23]
- **Queen Jane Approximately** (1 review): The first set's standout, with gritty Weir vocals and nice organ from Vince [21]
- **Smokestack Lightning** (1 review): Weir growls strong vocals while Garcia adds stylish, driving solos and fills [19]
- **One More Saturday Night** (1 review): Weir's energetic Saturday Night cuts off Garcia's emotional Dew, which the reviewer finds questionable [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1991-08-17.mtx.hansokolow.107826.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 19 songs; 156 min; rated 4.75/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd91-08-17.sbd.josephs.497.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 143 min; rated 4.23/5 by 13 [3]. Said about its sound: This recording does not include Wang Dang Doodle, which the reviewer wished it had [20]
- **gd1991-08-17.sbd.josephs.fix-497.20696.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 19 songs; 143 min [4]. Said about its sound: The earlier SHN set had sector boundary errors and extra chunks on every track, now fixed [4]
- **gd1991-08-17.sbd.lynn.81572.sbeok.flac48**: soundboard; 18 songs; 150 min [7]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended; screens on the lawn showed rain forest charity footage and psychedelic graphics [23]
- Reviewer ranks this Dew among the best, possibly the very best, of the 1990s [13]
- Dews as good as this one were rare in summer 1991 [14]
- Reviewer considers the show good but not great, and says the following night's show is much better [17]
- Reviewer's favorite Dew after Brent's death, and better than the one from 7/18/90 [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1991-08-17.mtx.hansokolow.107826.flac16**: transferred by hansokolow; source: Hansokolow matrix of these digital sources: SBD: shnid=20696 // AUD: shnid=94196 (Taped by: Keith Litzenberger) [1]
- **gd91-08-17.sbd.josephs.497.sbeok.shnf**: source: SBD -> DAT Master -> DAT Clone -> Tascam DA40 ->(SPDIF)-> SB Live -> SoundForge -> wav -> shn. [3]
- **gd1991-08-17.sbd.josephs.fix-497.20696.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by J. Josephs; source: SBD -> DAT Master -> DAT Clone -> Tascam DA40 ->(SPDIF)-> SB Live -> SoundForge -> wav -> shn [4]
- **gd1991-08-17.sbd.lynn.81572.sbeok.flac48**: transferred by Mark Lynn; source: Soundboard->DAT @ 48 kHz->DAT x 4.Conversion:Sony R500 ->M Audio Audiophile 2496 ->Soundforge (record)->CDWAV (track) ->FLAC [7]. Also: FLACs of the original 16-bit/48kHz recording, intended for DVD audio burning or archiving [7]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Play Dead: [Grateful Dead - 8-17-1991 Shoreline Amphitheatre Mountain View, CA](https://share.playdead.app/release/47797) [25]
